profile.headline: SWE II @ FreeWheel
profile.summary:
I’m a graduate CS student and HPC software engineer with a strong focus on Linux systems and high-performance C++ development. I work on optimizing scientific workloads, building tools for researchers, and supporting large-scale computing environments.

At Texas A&M High Performance Research Computing, I’ve benchmarked and tuned multi-core FFT and sparse matrix workloads using FFTW and Intel oneMKL, and I regularly work with Slurm, OpenMPI, and RHEL-based clusters. I’ve also helped researchers migrate complex workflows from Kubernetes to production HPC systems.

I enjoy building practical infrastructure and developer-facing tools, including Open OnDemand interactive apps for distributed GPU-based local LLM inference and automated machine learning pipelines.

My interests are in Linux performance engineering, parallel algorithms, distributed systems, and building software that runs efficiently at scale.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.locationName: College Station, Texas, United States · Remote
positions.description:
– Built and maintained backend systems for “College Football: Rapid Roster” iOS app (Swift, JavaScript, CloudKit JS)
– Scaled the app to thousands of active users and $2,500 monthly recurring revenue
– Developing a full-stack sports betting analytics platform that detects arbitrage, +EV, and middles opportunities
– Designed cloud deployment on AWS (Lambda, SQS, RDS/PostgreSQL, ECS/Fargate, ECR) using Docker, Git, and GitHub
Actions CI/CD for automated testing and production releases
– Implemented a C++ datafeed pipeline, a Go REST API backend, and a SwiftUI frontend

positions.title: Graduate Assistant Researcher (HPC Software Engineering)
positions.description:
– Benchmarked multi-core FFT and sparse matrix multiplication (FFTW, oneMKL) in C++on Intel Optane configured as swap;
analyzed performance tradeoffs for memory-bound HPC workloads
– Migrated Fermilab FPGA software simulation workflows from Kubernetes to Slurm, improving reproducibility and reducing
researcher setup overhead
– Co-authored peer-reviewed publication resulting from Fermilab collaboration: “wa-hls4ml: A Benchmark and Surrogate Models
for hls4ml Resource and Latency Estimation”, arXiv:2511.05615 (2025)
– Built and maintained an Open OnDemand interactive app for distributed LLM inference across multi-node jobs using Python;
version-controlled and managed releases using Git/GitHub; tracked feature development and sprint planning in Jira
– Shipped an Open OnDemand app to automate ML pipelines with AutoGluon on Slurm; standardized job specifications and reduced
experiment setup time
– Automated ticketing workflows by integrating Slack with the Slack API; developed a CLI workflow engine with structured Git-
based version control and collaborative code reviews on GitHub
– Resolved HPC support tickets across software troubleshooting, job scheduling, and environment configuration on Linux (RHEL 8) systems

positions.title: Student Technician
positions.description: backend developer for creating, updating, and maintaining ticket automation systems for High Performance Research Computing.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description:
– Built a Vue.js + Flask web app for segmenting and analyzing 8,861 retail outlets using Python and Pandas
– Developed a promotion recommendation algorithm generating 124,054 outlet-relevant promotions to confirm targeting and reduce
manual analysis
– Delivered an end-to-end analytics workflow that improved speed and consistency of sales planning decisions
